questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

He will not be able to attend the school function tomorrow, will you?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3 i.e Will you?**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8c9521921258ec6abc07d0cc2f42f7e8a9f276861eb6ba131097c2c69c56057.png] Explanation**

**Looking at the above sentence we find that:**

 
• The sentence uses a question tag in the end. 
 
• The sentence starts with 'He will not'
 
• Thus the question tag should be corelative to '**He will not**' and should have the pronoun **he**.
 
• Hence the question tag, in the end, will be '**Will ****he****?**'
 
• Thus it is clear that error lies in **Will you? **which is an incorrect usage. 

Thus the error lies in '**will you?' **which should be replaced with '**will he?' **Hence the correct answer is **Option 3 Will you?**

The correct statement will be: 'He will not be able to attend the school function tomorrow, **will he?**'

Mumbai has **a lot of** heritage structures which badly need restoration.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **O**ption 2 i.e No improvement

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a9d568b6419aa6ff37bbc42d94c53d413184d6cf8d7840be45cac8c3a302863.png] **Let's look at the following points-**

 
• In the given sentence, heritage structures(plural countable noun) is mentioned which needs maintenance.
 
• Let's take a look at the meaning of the phrase in the sentence. 
 
 
• **'A lot of' **can be used with **plural countable nouns **or** uncountable nouns**, affirmatives, negatives, and questions.

 **Example** -*That's a lot of money.*
 
 
 
• Hence we find that the sentence has no error and the correct phrase is used here which gives proper grammar to the sentence.

 

Therefore the correct answer is **Option 2 No improvement. **
